_comment: Single source-of-truth for VaultSigner's user-facing strings (spec §9). Keys are semantic (not raw English text) so ICU MessageFormat features like plurals/gender can be added per-key without renaming call sites. Generate platform-native formats from this file with i18n/generate-apple-strings.py (macOS) and i18n/generate-resx-strings.ps1 (Windows) rather than hand-editing .strings/.resx directly. All 13 macOS views and, as of item 3.7's full-app migration, every Windows page are migrated — see PROGRESS.md items 2.9/3.7 for the exact verification. Both generators emit every key in this file into their platform's native format regardless of which platform actually uses it. A few keys exist only for one platform's own UI shape (e.g. welcome.create_vault_button for Windows's inline vault-creation section, which macOS handles as a separate CreateVaultView/createvault.* screen instead, or createcompartment.* for Windows's standalone compartment-creation feature, which macOS doesn't have) — not every key is referenced by every platform's code. Product/brand names ("VaultSigner") are deliberately excluded, per standard i18n practice.
welcome.subtitle: Create a new vault, or open one you already have.
welcome.no_recent_vaults: No vaults yet — create one or open an existing file.
welcome.vault_unavailable_message: This vault's file couldn't be found at its remembered location. It may have been moved or deleted. You can forget this entry or re-locate the file.
welcome.open_section_header: Or open an existing vault file
manage_vaults.title: Manage Known Vaults
manage_vaults.subtitle: Vaults you've created or opened are remembered here so you don't have to browse for them again. Forgetting an entry never touches the file itself.
manage_vaults.add_panel_message: Choose a .vlt vault file to add to the list
manage_vaults.settings_footer: Close the current vault to switch to a different one, or manage which vaults are remembered.
import.title: Import Packet
import.subtitle: Choose a .vltkey or .vltpack file.
import.subtitle_detailed: Choose a .vltpack file exported from another VaultSigner vault (or a backup) to import its keys into this compartment.
import.transfer_password_prompt: This packet is protected by a transfer password.
duality.header: This import includes another vault's master key
duality.subtitle: Before any keys are merged, choose what to do with the incoming master key. This choice cannot be skipped.
duality.option1.title: Re-encrypt & discard incoming master key
duality.option1.description: Your keys will only need your existing master password. The imported vault's master password will not be kept.
duality.option1.no_unlocked_compartment: No compartment is currently unlocked to merge into.
duality.option2.title: Keep both master keys side by side
duality.option2.description: You'll keep two separate master passwords for this vault, one for each set of keys. Nothing is merged.
duality.option2.passphrase_field: New master passphrase for this compartment
duality.option3.title: Replace local master key with incoming master key
duality.option3.description: This will replace the password protecting ALL your existing keys, including ones you did not just import, with a different password. If you don't have both passwords available right now, stop.
duality.option3.no_unlocked_compartment: No compartment is currently unlocked to replace.
createvault.title: Create New Vault
createvault.master_passphrase_explanatio: The master passphrase protects your key list and labels, but not the keys themselves — each key gets its own independent passphrase when you create it.
createcompartment.title: New Compartment
createkey.title: Create Key
createkey.resource_placeholder: e.g. a hostname or service name
createkey.passphrase_placeholder: Required each time this key is used to sign
createkey.passphrase_explanation: This passphrase is independent of your vault's master passphrase — you'll need it again to sign or reveal this key.
unlock.title: Unlock Vault
keylist.no_keys_subtitle: Create your first key to start signing.
changepassphrase.title: Change Key Passphrase
revealkey.warning_text: This reveals the raw private key. Anyone who sees it can act as this key. It will not be copied to the clipboard automatically.
discardkey.title: Discard Key
discardkey.confirm_format: This permanently deletes "%@". Type "%@" to confirm.
exportpacket.include_master_explanation: Lets the recipient treat this as carrying its own master key (spec §5.2.1) instead of just independently-passphrased keys.
exportpacket.option_asis_detail: Keys stay encrypted with their own passphrases; no extra layer is added. **The label, description, and resource for each key travel in the clear inside this file.** Only use this if the recipient already knows each key's passphrase and the transport channel itself is trusted.
exportpacket.option_destination_title: Re-encrypt for the destination vault's master password
exportpacket.option_destination_detail: Choose this only if you know the master password of the vault you're importing into.
exportpacket.option_transfer_title: Protect with a one-time transfer password
exportpacket.option_transfer_detail: Set a new passphrase for this export only. Deliver it to the recipient through a separate channel from the file itself.
backupmasterkey.title: Back Up Master Key Only
backupmasterkey.warning_text: This alone does NOT protect anything — your per-key blobs are also required to actually use any key. Store this only alongside a plan for recovering those separately (e.g. this vault file itself, backed up elsewhere).
settings.title: Settings
settings.start_at_login_footer: Runs the background service that answers signing requests and FIDO2 prompts even when the VaultSigner window isn't open.
settings.auto_unlock_footer: Off by default. When on, this compartment's master passphrase is stored in the Keychain so it unlocks automatically at login, without you typing anything. This is weaker than the vault's normal design — see the confirmation dialog for what that means before turning it on.
settings.backup_footer: "Back up everything" protects all keys + the master key together (spec §5.4 recommends the one-time transfer password option for backups stored anywhere other than an already-encrypted local disk). "Master key only" is a shortcut for people who store key recovery material separately — on its own it does NOT protect anything, since the per-key blobs are also required.
settings.approve_login_item_message: Approve VaultSigner in System Settings → General → Login Items & Extensions
settings.login_item_not_found_message: Login item not found in this build (development build outside /Applications?)
settings.auto_unlock_incorrect_passphras: Incorrect master passphrase; auto-unlock was not enabled.
autounlockconfirm.title: Enable Auto-Unlock?
autounlockconfirm.body_text:
Your master passphrase will be stored in the macOS Keychain so this compartment unlocks automatically every time you log in or restart — no one needs to type anything.

This means a decryption path to your key list and labels now persists across a reboot without your input. It does not expose your keys themselves — each key still needs its own separate passphrase to sign or reveal. But anyone who can run code as you on this Mac may be able to read this stored passphrase too, similar to other Keychain-backed secrets.
